families.family: single_cookie_with_equals
families.why: The change was introduced with a docstring and a tiny refactor; the intended fast path is the common case of a short Cookie header containing a few well‑formed "name=value" pairs. Both versions allocate a dict once and strip only the parts that contain "=", so the new code should not be slower here.

def make(n):
    # n cookies "c0=v0;c1=v1;..."
    parts = [f'c{i}=v{i}' for i in range(n)]
    header = ';'.join(parts)
    return [[header]]

families.family: many_well_formed_cookies
families.why: Typical cookie headers contain many key=value pairs. The change moves the strip outside the equality test, which the author likely expected to avoid repeated attribute look‑ups and make the hot path tighter.

families.family: well‑formed cookie header – each part contains a "=" and no surrounding whitespace
families.why: The new code strips each part before the "=" test; when every part already has an "=" and no spaces the extra strip is a no‑op, so the fast‑path of the original (strip‑then‑split) and the new (strip‑then‑split) take the same time. families.family: repeated_same_ipv4
families.why: The same public IPv4 address is checked many times; the added LRU cache turns the first miss into a hit for all subsequent calls, so the head version should be faster.
families.size_meaning: Number of repeated checks (n) – the generator returns up to 8 identical calls, cost grows with n because the caller will repeat the list n times.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    ip = "20.0.0.1"          # public, not in EXCLUDE_RANGES
    # return up to 8 identical argument lists; the harness can repeat the list n times
    return [[ip] for _ in range(min(n, 8))]

families.family: Repeated identical IP address – the cache should turn the second and later calls into O(1) look‑ups.
families.why: The added @lru_cache stores the result after the first evaluation. Subsequent calls with the same argument hit the cache and avoid the ipaddress parsing + overlap loop entirely.
families.size_meaning: Number of calls (n) – the first call does the full work, the remaining n‑1 calls are cache hits.

families.family: repeated_same_ip
families.why: The new version adds an LRU cache. When the same IP address is checked many times, the first call does the full overlap scan and subsequent calls are O(1) cache hits. The base version repeats the full scan every time.
families.size_meaning: Number of calls (n) – we emit up to 8 calls, each with the identical address.

def make(n):
    # repeat the same public, non‑excluded IPv4 address
    ip = "8.8.8.8"
    calls = min(n, 8)
    return [[ip] for _ in range(calls)]

families.family: unique_ipv4
families.why: Every call receives a distinct, valid public IPv4 address. The cache never hits, so each call pays the extra dictionary lookup, hashing, and LRU bookkeeping on top of the original overlap test.
families.size_meaning: Number of distinct IPs (n) – the generator returns up to 8 different IPs; the harness can repeat the list to reach n total calls.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    base = 20_000_001          # 20.0.0.1 as integer
    ips = []
    for i in range(min(n, 8)):
        # construct a.b.c.d from integer
        val = base + i
        a = (val >> 24) & 0xFF
        b = (val >> 16) & 0xFF
        c = (val >> 8) & 0xFF
        d = val & 0xFF
        ips.append([f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"])
    return ips
